doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

title: Ike Day's illness and the swinging Flame band of 1954
summary: Ike Day is dying of TB while Griffin, Clean Head, Junior Mance and Ware work the Flame and Basin Street, with Hawkins and Webster dropping in.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Then in '54, at the same time Ike Day died, I think that was in '54 when he passed away. In fact, that was when the doctor told him he had TB and told him if he didn't stop playing, it would kill him, and Ike said, "Well, I been playing all my life and that's the way I'm gonna die." And he almost did. It got so he would get on a bandstand, and on one session, you'd get him playing and his feet would swell up so bad, we'd have to help him up off the drums.
But there was a new era coming and all that next

year in '54 -- that was when Johnny Griffin, Clean Head, Junior Mance, Jimmy Matz, Buddy Smith and myself were working for this same guy at the Flame; he had 2 clubs. The Flame and Basin Street -- right there in Chicago. And oh boy, we used to have swinging times. Tune Up, Clean Head's tune; Johnny Griffin playing his butt off -- I remember seeing Stan Colemang Hawkins and Ben Webster in the club one night -- that was an experience.
them, I didn't talk to him. Like I said, I was always shy with those big names.
